subject: clownfish
title: Clownfish Survive Heatwaves by Getting Smaller, as Couples

scenes.text: Some adult clownfish got smaller. On purpose.
Scientists in Papua New Guinea measured wild clownfish every month. Many got shorter, some several times.
That year, a heatwave pushed the water about four degrees Celsius above normal.
Seventy-one percent of females and seventy-nine percent of males shrank at least once.
A smaller body needs less food when heat makes food scarce. Shrinking raised survival odds by up to seventy-eight percent.
And the best survivors didn't shrink alone. They shrank together with their partner.

description:
A 2025 Science Advances study tracked wild Amphiprion percula clownfish in Kimbe Bay, Papua New Guinea, during a 2023 marine heatwave about 4 C above average.
100 of 134 fish shrank at least once, shrinking raised survival chances by as much as 78%, and fish that shrank alongside their breeding partner did best.
Did you know fish could shrink?
first_comment: Divers measured each fish with calipers in under 30 seconds, then let it go. 41% of the shrinkers did it more than once. Should Finding Nemo get a sequel about this?
